title: Vedas, Upanishads and the Bhagavad Gita
welcome_lead: From the Rig Veda's hymns to Krishna's counsel on the battlefield, encounter Hinduism's sacred texts.
meta_desc: Religious Studies Adventure: Vedas, Upanishads and the Bhagavad Gita.
final_note: You have heard ancient hymns and modern devotion. Hindu scripture is vast and layered.

walkthroughs.body_html: The four Vedas — Rig, Sama, Yajur and Atharva — span hymns, melodies, sacrificial formulas and household rituals. Composed in archaic Sanskrit, they are 'shruti' (heard) and were transmitted orally with extraordinary precision long before being written.

The principal Upanishads (e.g. Brihadaranyaka, Chandogya, Katha) developed philosophical reflection on Brahman, atman, karma and moksha from around 800-200 BCE. They inspired the Vedanta schools and continue to influence Hindu thought worldwide.

The Bhagavad Gita, set on the eve of the Kurukshetra battle, presents Krishna's teaching to Arjuna on dharma, action and devotion. It integrates karma, bhakti and jnana paths and remains the most widely read Hindu scripture, central to figures from Gandhi to modern teachers.
